milestones.title: Make perception and action belong to the body
milestones.what: The roadmap set the Pluck Test as the boundary: communication can detach, but perception, reasoning and execution should remain with Nova. It also proposed retiring older memory and motor scaffolding.
milestones.why: A chat application owning Nova's execution would take her ability to act with it when removed.
milestones.tradeoff: Body ownership improves independence, but moving code is insufficient: callbacks, state and context must also have working headless paths.
milestones.verification: This records the decision. It does not claim every item in the roadmap was implemented; nova_memory still exists in the current map.

milestones.title: Separate specialist selection from adapter loading
milestones.what: The KoELS finding distinguishes switching among preloaded adapters from adding a new adapter that requires a model restart. It proposes a working set instead of loading every specialist.
milestones.why: VRAM is limited, and choosing an expert should not assume the inference server can load arbitrary new adapter files without restarting.
milestones.tradeoff: Fast selection within a loaded set comes with a slower, coordinated path for changing that set.
milestones.verification: The report explicitly left exact-build flash-attention and VRAM checks open. This is the historical finding, not a current vendor capability claim.

refs.contains: ## Constraints that shape the equip design

milestones.title: Extract the runtime from the conversation interface
milestones.what: NovaRuntime takes ownership of the wake loop, model dispatch, perception, indexer and service control. The chat interface subscribes to events and supplies output callbacks.
milestones.why: Nova needed to continue running without one particular chat application, and KoELS needed body-owned model lifecycle control.
milestones.tradeoff: Callbacks decouple the body from a specific UI, but the host still supplies important context and coordination. The report itself lists unfinished headless parity work.
milestones.verification: The report distinguishes early live checks from steps that were then only built or tested. A later June 10 report records additional verification.

milestones.title: Headless boot gets a recorded live verification
milestones.what: A headless test first failed because required packages were absent from the import path. The entry point was fixed; the report then records model startup, indexing and generations without a chat server attached.
milestones.why: Moving the wake loop into a new package did not by itself guarantee that a standalone process could import and run it.
milestones.tradeoff: A successful boot proves one path worked then. It does not prove identical context, persistence or behavior across every host today.
milestones.verification: Attributed to the June 10 report. The atlas has not rerun that live test.

milestones.title: Change the model and leave room for adapters
milestones.what: The upgrade document selects the repository's Qwen 3.6 27B Q6_K_XL setup with thinking and MTP configuration.
milestones.why: The recorded goal was generation speed with memory headroom for speculative decoding and KoELS adapters.
milestones.tradeoff: Model, quantization, launch flags and adapter compatibility are coupled; changing one requires checking the actual inference process.
milestones.verification: This records the chosen configuration and motivation. Performance claims in the historical document are not new measurements by the atlas.

milestones.title: A large apparent change was timestamp churn
milestones.what: The postmortem attributes the June 27 burst to automatic header restamps and line-ending changes rather than a new source-development session.
milestones.why: The sync watcher was repeatedly committing generated metadata. Timestamp interpretation also confused UTC and Korea time.
milestones.tradeoff: Frequent backups preserve work, but their commit count is not a measure of engineering activity. This timeline filters net header-only changes separately.
milestones.verification: The historical report says 1,325 automatic commits and no behavioral source change for that incident. The timeline independently compares before/after content.

milestones.title: Fix duplicate replies and the idle action path
milestones.what: The report traces repeated replies to the FOR COLE promotion path and records time/turn-taking checks plus missing generation-trace events. It separately addresses idle wakes that reflected without doing the next action.
milestones.why: The same human exchange was being answered again through later autonomous promotions. String similarity missed paraphrases, and missing trace events hid the extra path.
milestones.tradeoff: Generation coordination needs explicit ownership and receipts; adding more prompt instructions cannot repair a missing execution branch.
milestones.verification: The report says the fixes needed a restart. Its claim is historical, not proof of the code loaded in a process now.

milestones.title: Remove resident paid mentors and move sight to the local model
milestones.what: The report removes automatic paid chat participants and the cloud vision path, retaining a retirement message for old mentor directives.
milestones.why: The recorded request was to stop those API costs and use Nova's own multimodal model for sight.
milestones.tradeoff: Local inference keeps that work on the machine, while retirement stubs help old references fail clearly. Later optional cloud witness work is a separate decision.
milestones.verification: A historical removal report; it should not be generalized into a current claim that no optional cloud boundary exists.

milestones.title: Let memories evolve and separate the archive from the live conversation
milestones.what: The memory store adds retention for a small group of similar text memories instead of dropping every near-duplicate. Recalled material is explicitly labeled as a past archive, and indexer status describes which process it can actually observe.
milestones.why: The dated comments explain that one similarity threshold could not distinguish an evolving thought from a different moment on the same topic. They also record that old archived dialogue was being mistaken for the current exchange.
milestones.tradeoff: Similarity-based retention can still remove useful older records. Archive wording helps distinguish past text, but successful retrieval still has to reach the intended prompt. A status check in a separate process cannot prove the server worker is absent.
milestones.verification: The July 19 retained before/after diff and current dated source comments were inspected for this atlas. No memory writes, retention experiment or live recall test was performed.

milestones.title: Protect the live conversation from oversized background context
milestones.what: A passover records that context trimming could drop the entire live conversation when always-loaded material grew too large. The session added a floor for recent turns and investigated witness wiring.
milestones.why: Nova could answer from old background material while the actual user exchange was missing from the request.
milestones.tradeoff: Keeping recent turns preserves the current interaction but does not solve the cost of carrying large amounts of background context.
milestones.verification: Recorded in the July 21 session report. Use current source and a live request trace before diagnosing today's behavior.

refs.contains: Context trim was dropping the ENTIRE live conversation

milestones.title: Give the witness an explicit evidence-reading option
milestones.what: The witness's verdict menu was changed to include verification reads; evidence gathered by the witness was carried across rounds within a turn.
milestones.why: Inviting the model to check evidence mid-prompt was ineffective when its final legal choices were only PASS or CONCERN.
milestones.tradeoff: Verification can improve grounding, but it adds latency and needs an explicit read-only execution path plus observable results.
milestones.verification: The report cites a first witness_verified event at 09:59:19 on July 22. This is attributed historical evidence.

milestones.title: Propose a smaller, more deliberate context budget
milestones.what: The context-diet document proposes recent journal tails, a shaped workspace summary and a compact drives view. It also describes a risk of silently omitting a trailing identity file.
milestones.why: Large and frequently changing background blocks consumed context capacity and prefill time before the conversation began.
milestones.tradeoff: Retrieval and summaries reduce the always-present payload, but change what information is immediately available to the model.
milestones.verification: The document explicitly calls itself a decision discussion. The atlas does not convert its proposed items into completed features.

milestones.title: Evaluate a separate witness engine and a deferred second opinion
milestones.what: The surviving report compares a small local auditor with the main model and records an optional deferred cloud escalation. Its small-model replay results did not justify replacing the main auditor automatically.
milestones.why: Checking claims on the same large model can add latency; a faster judge is useful only if it still catches the relevant errors.
milestones.tradeoff: Lower latency and a separate process do not establish equivalent judgment. The evaluation harness and live witness are different components.
milestones.verification: The local report contains damaged/null-padded text. Only its surviving passages support this summary; the missing beginning is not reconstructed.

milestones.title: Provision a separate desktop for the computer faculty
milestones.what: The provisioning script describes a Linux desktop, VNC/noVNC services and a dedicated X display for the computer environment.
milestones.why: A stable target desktop gives the computer backend somewhere to run GUI actions and capture results.
milestones.tradeoff: Provisioning a desktop is distinct from wiring it into the ordinary reasoning/action loop. The map keeps those claims separate.
milestones.verification: The date comes from the source header. It is not a newly performed provisioning or end-to-end embodiment test.

milestones.title: Make the architecture inspectable at three levels
milestones.what: The atlas adds a simple mental map, a source-level inspection view and a local live watcher with source-linked explanations.
milestones.why: The project had grown beyond what could reliably be held in one person's memory. Source wiring needed to be visible without expanding detachable tool internals.
milestones.tradeoff: Static extraction updates structural facts; the meaning of dynamic connections still needs reviewed explanations.
milestones.verification: Recorded in the atlas decision notes. This entry describes the atlas, not a change to Nova's running faculties.

milestones.title: Connect architecture to its history and engineering reasoning
milestones.what: Add the timeline, component learning guides, step-through flows, impact exploration and a review queue.
milestones.why: Cole asked for a durable way to catch up on forgotten decisions, understand why the parts exist and build on them with confidence.
milestones.tradeoff: History must distinguish decisions from implementation and old verification from present behavior. Unknown motivations stay unknown.
milestones.verification: See the atlas's own validation record; no Nova runtime behavior is changed by this feature.
